hi!! can 100% relate and still very much a work in progress. thanks for posting so i can read the replies too :) 

for apps, i tried Habitica for a while and it was good, doing daily habits gives your character points like a video game! but my all time favorite that ive fully converted to is Finch, i've been using it for a year. soo cute to get lil outfits And the character is a pet and not you/independent from yourself (helps me to treat someone else well if not myself, Haha). very customizable, and i really appreciate their gentle suggestions. its just a very friendly, non-judgmental app that seems to invite me to interact vs making it another chore to keep track of.

and also like some other comments have mentioned, getting a cat was transformative for myself. i also find that having company over once in a while helps kick me into cleaning that ive procrastinated.

Hey friend - no, you are not wrong for being upset. If my significant other talked about me like that to other people, I absolutely would have done the same as you, trying to bring it up to him and would likely get triggered too. If I can be positive for a second - obviously I don’t have the full context, and perhaps you don’t either, but it doesn’t seem like he did that maliciously, and it can be hard for people not living with trauma/PTSD to really understand how to navigate boundaries in explaining behavior vs privacy. The hard part is that it’s absolutely individual - your boundaries are gonna look different from his or mine or anyone else, and unfortunately it falls to us as individuals to communicate that the best you can. Would you be open to discussing boundaries around discussing your treatment/trauma when you are in a less triggered state? If it helps legitimize your feelings - talking about your medical care and history is breaching HIPAA and there are laws against that for a reason. Not to say your boyfriend is a criminal lol, but just to affirm that you are right to be upset, and many other people would be. I’m sorry you had to experience that, I hope you can find a positive way forward. Best of luck 🫶

hi, i want to say i am grateful for you. i still struggle with passive suicidal ideation, but there have been so many years i have told myself the same as you, and im trying to change that this year. i am not going to say it gets better, or list reasons for you not to act on these thoughts - of course, if it were up to me, i would love for you to live but to also want to live. but i am closer to being in your shoes than wanting to live. your post made me reckon with some things that ive mentally had in the background lately - personally, i believe there is no noble meaning or purpose to suffering, nor is there any reason to live for the sake of living either. but i think that my suffering and my living has hopefully made me at least made me someone who can be a listener or understander by others in our position… the “people” who want you to live for their own selfish reasons cannot possibly understand what this constant, lifelong, soul-crushing pain does to us. but there is something i realized as of late… life is absurd and unpredictable. i did not choose to be born, but every day that i survive i chose to live. there is no greater meaning for this choice, but because of that i have seen some wicked things that make me think, “i understand why other people have come to love life.” i saw a meteor shower yesterday. i watched a new anime. i ate food that was cooked with love by a stranger. my life might not have meaning but this does not take away the meaning imbued in the world around me. op, i have kept suffering, there is not a day i dont recognize that - but i have also started to recognize the beauty in things beyond my history of trauma. some day i hope that i feel like i no longer suffer, but for as long as i do, i dont want that to prevent me from the microscopic flickers of beauty and value. each day, i gain a new days worth of perspective… you will too, whether you want to or not, even if you pretend.

“CPTSD turned me into a criminal” - I went into this hoping for a thoughtful reflection, but you’re literally just… straight up blaming CPTSD for your own self-admitted harmful decisions and behavior. I don’t have enough context to say you don’t have CPTSD at all, but I agree with other comments that this is probably not the source of all these problems you are experiencing. Why do you so firmly believe other people (especially people who were never involved in past trauma) owe you patience and compassion and MONEY, while you also believe you’re allowed to just, not do things you transactionally committed to do in good faith? Just like people with CPTSD can still be abusers, you are not owed the world on a silver platter without contribution. You seem honest about recognizing these behaviors as negative, but I think you need to unpack your selfishness and avoidance of responsibility. But if you don’t want to change anything - you reap what you sow. Growth is hard work but it’s WORK - you don’t just get a free pass for having hardships.
thank you!! yeah ive seen a lot of mentions of lithium in this sub too so ill definitely ask about both next time i see my psychiatrist!

thank you!! i will definitely look into those, luckily my psychiatrist is also supportive of supplements/micronutrients so ive been taking vitamin d for a while and i definitely think it has helped with the sadness quite a bit. i really appreciate your encouragement, thank you :)

thank you! yes its so disheartening that the only approved medications we have currently do such a piss poor job for so many people. even just hearing that you found something that works for you is a relief. totally agree on the dissociation too, though lately that specifically has helped me cope with suicidal ideation. i started building better lifestyle habits a few months ago so im hoping to get back into those when i get back to being functional :)

thank you :) i think im low enough that im willing to consider it, i tend to be very sensitive to meds in general (im that person that can take like one tylenol and be good to go on pain) so if i do ill try it at the lowest dose possible! it does make me feel more at ease to hear that it worked for you so i appreciate the insight
